knowledge:
- key_parameters: genedata=A data.frame with three columns (gsname, gene [numeric Entrez GeneID], weight [1 for activated, -1 for repressed]) specifying the input gene sets ;; pattern=A data.frame with four columns (gsname, acttype ["High" or "Low"], cotype ["Norm", "Quantile", or "Exprs"], cutoff [numeric value]) specifying the activity pattern of interest ;; chipdata=The expression compendium to search, either 'moe4302' (mouse GPL1261) or 'hgu133a' (human GPL96) ;; Pval.co=Significance cutoff (adjusted p-value) for reporting active biological contexts ;; directory=An optional directory path; if specified, GSCA automatically runs recursive follow-up analyses for all significant experiments and saves the outputs ;; N=The number of top-ranked biological contexts to highlight in GSCAplot (maximum of 5) ;; Ordering=The ordering method used in GSCAeda (e.g., "Average")
- alternatives: GSCAui=An interactive Shiny-based user interface recommended for users who prefer a graphical interface, easier customization of plots, and more powerful analysis options ;; CisGenome/RMA/limma=Upstream tools recommended for processing raw ChIP-seq and microarray data to generate the input gene lists
- when_to_use: Use when you have identified a set of activated and repressed target genes for a transcription factor (or other biological pathway) and want to systematically scan public expression datasets to discover tissues, cell types, or disease states where this regulatory program is active.
- pitfalls: Different transcription factors behave differently, meaning there is no single optimal cutoff value for the activity pattern; users must experiment with cutoff stringency ;; Setting the directory parameter to a non-NULL path in the main GSCA function triggers recursive tabSearch and GSCAeda runs for all significant experiments, which can generate a very large number of files and take a long time to complete ;; Gene IDs in the genedata data frame must be numeric Entrez GeneIDs, not gene symbols ;; Every unique geneset name defined in genedata must appear exactly once in the pattern data frame.

workflows.name: gsca_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify and visualize biological contexts (cell types, tissues, or diseases) enriched with a specific gene set activity pattern.
input: genedata.csv (Data frame containing gene set names, Entrez Gene IDs, and activation/repression weights)
pattern.csv (Data frame defining the target activity direction, cutoff type, and cutoff value for each gene set)
workflows.stages: 1. Format the gene set data and weights into the required three-column data frame structure ;; 2. Define the target activity pattern and cutoffs in a four-column data frame ;; 3. Run the enrichment search across the selected compendium using GSCA ;; 4. Visualize the top-ranked biological contexts using GSCAplot
workflows.code:
library(GSCA)
data(Oct4ESC_TG)
activenum <- length(Oct4ESC_TG[[1]])
repressnum <- length(Oct4ESC_TG[[2]])
Octgenedata <- data.frame(
      gsname=c("TF",rep("TG",activenum+repressnum)),
      gene=c(18999,Oct4ESC_TG[[1]],Oct4ESC_TG[[2]]),
      weight=c(rep(1,1+activenum),rep(-1,repressnum)),
      stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
Octpattern <- data.frame(
      gsname=c("TF","TG"),
      acttype="High",
      cotype="Norm",
      cutoff=0.1,
      stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
displayoct <- Octoutput <- GSCA(Octgenedata,Octpattern,"moe4302",Pval.co=0.05,directory=NULL)
GSCAplot(Octoutput,N=5,plotfile=NULL,Title="GSCA plot of Oct4 in ESC")

workflows.name: gsca_followup_eda
workflows.intent: Perform targeted exploratory data analysis and statistical comparisons on specific experiments or contexts of interest.
input: genedata.csv (Data frame containing gene set names, Entrez Gene IDs, and activation/repression weights)
pattern.csv (Data frame defining the target activity direction, cutoff type, and cutoff value)
keyword (A character string representing an Experiment ID or keyword to search the compendium)
workflows.stages: 1. Format the gene set data and target activity pattern ;; 2. Search the compendium for matching experiments or samples using tabSearch ;; 3. Perform pairwise t-tests and generate activity boxplots/heatmaps across the retrieved contexts using GSCAeda
workflows.code:
library(GSCA)
data(STAT1_TG)
Statgenenum <- length(STAT1_TG)
Statgenedata <- data.frame(gsname=c("TF",rep("TG",Statgenenum)),gene=c(6772,STAT1_TG),weight=1,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
Statpattern <- data.frame(gsname=c("TF","TG"),acttype="High",cotype="Norm",cutoff=0.1,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
GSE7123out <- tabSearch("GSE7123","hgu133a")
GSE7123followup <- GSCAeda(Statgenedata,Statpattern,"hgu133a",GSE7123out,Pval.co=0.05,Ordering="Average",Title=NULL,outputdir=NULL) 
GSE7123followup$Tstats
GSE7123followup$Pval
